note: Triennial election of the rural district council, polled 27 May 1908; "there were only six contests". Ballyards (Andrew Davidson, George Brown, Thomas Quinn, senr., nominated) is not in the results; the Irish News says the Nationalists gained a seat there, but the members returned were not found, so it is not filed. The nomination list marks candidates "a" (against direct labour) or "d l" (direct labour); these are not party labels and are not filed as such. Returned unopposed. James H. Stronge: no party label printed in 1908. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Middletown, Armagh County Council, 25 May 1905, printed 'U': Armagh Guardian, 2 June 1905, p. 5 ("Council Elections: 2 Unionist Gains, 1 Nationalist"); candidates in the Armagh Guardian, 28 April 1905, p. 5 ("Nominations: County Councillors"); Middletown, Armagh County Council, 27 May 1908, printed 'U.': Northern Whig, 6 June 1908, p. 10 ("Provincial Elections: County Councils: Armagh"); candidates in the Newry Reporter, 2 May 1908, p. 10 ("Armagh County Council": the nominations)).
